beforeAfter.before: Ungated kernel (same tree, fixture present, gate absent): a real TaskAddressSpace::Domain task through handle_syscall could allocate a grant (domain-owned frames published USER in the SAS root), receive a raw receiver mapping with shared_to's rights ignored, and the run leaked frames — S22-RV64-GRANT-GATE-{ALLOC,REGISTER,SHARE,SLICE,FRAMES}: FAIL, exit 1 (.logs/native-domain-qemu/h1-grant-gate-6j4WCL). AArch64/x86_64 Tier-2 admission was enabled in development images, and snapshot capture/restore was reachable with a writer/reader checksum and layout mismatch and no all-hart quiescence.
beforeAfter.after: Every grant entry point that names a private-root task refuses at the common syscall gate with the per-op alloc-safe sentinel (0 / usize::MAX / PermissionDenied) before any table row, PTE, pin or frame exists; SAS→SAS Tier-1 grants and copied IPC are proven unchanged. Non-RV64 Tier-2 admission and warm snapshot are fail-closed by policy, with the posture logged at boot and stale snapshot headers invalidated on a gated image. Architectural tags come from a bounded live pool: two live roots can never share a tag, exhaustion refuses the domain, and a released tag is reissued only after its invalidation completed.
